description: New kitchen, new bath/shower room in basement, installation of new ventilation units and extractors, repoint lime plaster window wells, replacement back door, new boiler, rewiring, new flooring, replace skirtings repairs to downpipes and gutters, lime plastering/painting and associated works.
decision_conditions:
The following list is information, details and plans which would need to be provided at a minimum to allow for assessment of any future application:

•	Elevation drawings should be provided showing in appropriate detail the external works proposed.
•	A comprehensive and appropriately detailed Heritage Impact Statement, Internal and External Schedule of works and Methodology Statement
•	Basement ventilation system – confirmation of details of the proposed ventilation brick and its exact location drawn on elevation drawings 
•	Extractor fan – details of the proposed ventilation block (cast iron or brick ventilation block concealing extractor fan) and its exact location also on elevational drawings
•	Conversion of basement hallway to bathroom – Details of fixtures and fittings, information about the proposed partitioning and its construction eg materials - type of wood, how it will be fixed etc
•	Windows – submission of a methodology plan to show how repairs are intended to be carried out. Any removal/repair of windows should be explained in the heritage statement (or methodology).
•	New doors need to be detailed in drawings. The new bathroom door for example should probably match the existing doors in the building to maintain consistency. Existing and proposed designs should therefore be illustrated in drawings. The proposed drawing details provided for the external replacement door is not sufficiently detailed. 
•	The boiler is acceptable in principle but two locations are provided. Appropriate plans should be provided which show a singular proposed location including how it will be installed to minimise impact on historic fabric. The location in the orangery is likely to be acceptable rather than the principle living room, however appropriate justification and assessment should be provided in a heritage statement.  
•	Details regarding flooring, decorative skirting, guttering need to be provided. This needs all be set out and explained in the heritage statement regarding location, material and design and/or indicated on drawings (for example are wooden floors being removed and replaced or are they being covered with carpet etc, will the guttering be cast iron or PVC). If skirting is being added what kind of design and what location. 

Reference should be made to Council's Validation Checklist for further details:
https://www.richmond.gov.uk/media/18491/local_validation_checklist_for_all_applications.pdf
